title: Apostates - a hidden population for potential trauma and abuse - with Hari Parekh

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚到除了出卖时间换取金钱之外的收入，那会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士（Dr. Marianne Trent），自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性的收入来源。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要告诉大家。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特（Sophie Foote）的“一对多”（One-to-Many）项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员制服务和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己是在2022年完成该项目的，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的成长历程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的推荐链接加入，你将获得苏菲提供的奖励，以及我额外提供的独家支持套餐，无需支付额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四场小组智囊团会议、大师课、个性化指导、一份Fortnum and Mason的礼品，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 请通过描述中链接的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时为你解答。

sentences.en: If you're looking to become a psychologist, then let this be your guide.
sentences.zh: 如果你正寻求成为一名心理学家，那么让这成为你的指南吧。

sentences.en: With this podcast at your side, you'll be on your way to the Aspiring Psychologist podcast with Dr. Marianne Trens.
sentences.zh: 有了这个播客在身边，你将走上成为玛丽安·特伦特博士的“有抱负的心理学家”播客之路。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听“有抱负的心理学家”播客。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening and thank you for being part of my world.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们的收听，也感谢你们成为我世界的一部分。

sentences.en: Today is episode 43 and I will level with you.
sentences.zh: 今天是第43期，我要和大家交个底。

sentences.en: This episode was always going to be happening, but this is not quite the episode I had planned.
sentences.zh: 这一期节目本来是一定会出的，但它并不是我原计划中的那一期。

sentences.en: But yeah, the one I had planned is coming soon.
sentences.zh: 不过，我原计划的那一期很快就会发布了。

sentences.en: But yeah, there's just been a slight delay.
sentences.zh: 只是稍微推迟了一点。

sentences.en: But yeah, I am today using some old footage.
sentences.zh: 今天我用的是一些旧素材。

sentences.en: But it's really an incredible interview that I'd done and really very interesting.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一次非常棒的采访，内容也非常有趣。

sentences.en: And it's with Harry Parekh.
sentences.zh: 采访对象是哈里·帕雷克（Harry Parekh）。

sentences.en: And he is now a third year trainee.
sentences.zh: 他现在是一名三年级的实习生。

sentences.en: Whereas when we met to do the interview, I believe he was getting interviews for training.
sentences.zh: 而我们采访时，我相信他当时正在参加实习面试。

sentences.en: He might well have just been told he had a place on training, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他可能刚接到通知说他获得了实习名额。

sentences.en: So it was interesting to listen back to this episode because I think I've become a better podcaster over the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: 回听这一期节目很有意思，因为我觉得过去几年我作为播客主变得更好了。

sentences.en: And yeah, it just feels like a lot has changed in my life, you know, since then.
sentences.zh: 而且，自从那时起，我的生活确实发生了很大变化，你知道的。

sentences.en: So I've just checked and we got this published in May 2020.
sentences.zh: 我刚才查了一下，这期节目是在2020年5月发布的。

sentences.en: So yeah, it's, you know, coming up almost two and a half years ago, probably since we filmed it.
sentences.zh: 所以，距离我们拍摄它大概已经过去快两年半了。

sentences.en: And loads has changed, you know, what we know is that we were in a much earlier stage of the pandemic at that time.
sentences.zh: 发生了很多变化，我们都知道，那时我们还处于疫情的早期阶段。

sentences.en: And I was filming on my NHS laptop at that time.
sentences.zh: 当时我是在我的NHS（英国国家医疗服务体系）笔记本电脑上拍摄的。

sentences.en: And then it all got stuck on there and we couldn't get it off.
sentences.zh: 后来视频都卡在里面了，我们取不出来。

sentences.en: So we could only get the sound off.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只能导出音频。

sentences.en: So despite the fact we had filmed ourselves, it was stuck.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们拍摄了视频，但它被锁住了。

sentences.en: And so we couldn't, we couldn't access the video.
sentences.zh: 所以我们无法访问视频文件。

sentences.en: And so it was, yeah, just audio only.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，只能是纯音频。

sentences.en: And we're keeping it audio only today because I don't have any additional video.
sentences.zh: 今天我们也保持纯音频形式，因为我没有额外的视频。

sentences.en: But you can definitely watch it on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 但你绝对可以在YouTube上观看。

sentences.en: If you do like to access your podcasts that way, there will be a blog post coming soon as well.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢通过那种方式收听播客，很快也会有一篇博客文章发布。

sentences.en: But it's not quite ready yet, but it will be coming soon.
sentences.zh: 虽然还没完全准备好，但很快就会上线。

sentences.en: So I thought this was a really interesting episode to bring to your awareness as aspiring psychologists,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这一期节目对于作为有抱负的心理学家的你们来说非常值得关注，

sentences.en: because the term apostate wasn't one that I was aware of.
sentences.zh: 因为“叛教者”（apostate）这个词我之前并不了解。

sentences.en: And it's a hidden research population, but also potentially a hidden trauma population too.
sentences.zh: 这是一个隐藏的研究群体，但也可能是一个隐藏的创伤群体。

sentences.en: So I won't say too much more about it, but I hope you find this really interesting and really inspiring.
sentences.zh: 我就不多说了，希望你们觉得这期节目既有趣又鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: So I will catch you on the other side.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们稍后再见。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So hi, I'm Dr. Marianne Trent and I'm a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，我是一名临床心理学家。

sentences.en: I've got a keen interest in research and I spotted some really interesting research just yesterday, actually.
sentences.zh: 我对研究有着浓厚的兴趣，事实上，就在昨天，我发现了一些非常有趣的研究。

sentences.en: And it got me very excited.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And so I reached out to the person that's written the research and he's here with me today.
sentences.zh: 所以我联系了这项研究的作者，他今天也和我在一起。

sentences.en: I'll let him introduce himself.
sentences.zh: 我让他自己介绍一下。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Harry Parekh.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫哈里·帕雷克。

sentences.en: I wrote the research study on apostates as a hidden population of abuse victims, which was published in January of this year.
sentences.zh: 我撰写了关于“叛教者作为隐藏的虐待受害者群体”的研究报告，该报告于今年1月发表。

sentences.en: I've got around four years experience working in psychology.
sentences.zh: 我在心理学领域有大约四年的工作经验。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I've got my stripes.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我已经积累了一些经验。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Oh, honestly, I'm so excited to speak to you.
sentences.zh: 哦，说实话，我太兴奋能和你交谈了。

sentences.en: Um, I predominantly worked in adult mental health, but also children and families.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我主要在成人心理健康领域工作，但也涉及儿童和家庭领域。

sentences.en: So, um, I was surprised to learn of a really big, interesting word that I had no idea what it is.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我很惊讶地学到了一个非常重要且有趣的词，我之前完全不知道它是什么。

sentences.en: Even to look at it on paper, I was like, I don't even know how to say that.
sentences.zh: 即使在纸上看到它，我也在想，我甚至不知道该怎么读它。

sentences.en: Can you take us through what, what it is?
sentences.zh: 你能带我们了解一下它是什么吗？

sentences.en: So apostate is, is a big word.
sentences.zh: “叛教者”是一个很大的词。

sentences.en: And it's, it's the way that the, it's the way that the religious kind of describe, it's a, it's a term used by the religious to describe people raised within religious families who
sentences.zh: 这是宗教界用来描述那些在宗教家庭中长大的人的术语，他们

sentences.en: once identified as religious, but have now ceased to believe in the existence of a God, gods, or follow that religious belief.
sentences.zh: 曾经认同宗教，但现在不再相信上帝或神灵的存在，也不再遵循那种宗教信仰。

sentences.en: So, and then they now identify as non-religious.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们现在认同自己是非宗教人士。

sentences.en: So it's the people that have gone from being religious and non-religious.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是那些从有宗教信仰转变为无宗教信仰的人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So there's not like a tick box option on forms that we see as yet saying apostate, apostate.
sentences.zh: 所以我们目前在表格上还没有看到“叛教者”这个选项，对吧？

sentences.en: Um, but it's, you'd sort of like that you'd go for like no religion or.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但你可能会选“无宗教信仰”之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You go for no religion or you go for atheist or you go for, you know, other, um, I think it's, it's one of those terms which isn't really widely used or really widely recognized.
sentences.zh: 你会选“无宗教信仰”，或者“无神论者”，或者“其他”。嗯，我认为这是一个并没有被广泛使用或广泛认可的术语。

sentences.en: Um, it's kind of used as a, as a, as a kind of label used by the religious to negatively sometimes associate somebody with that word.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它有时被宗教人士用作一种标签，用来负面地关联某人。

sentences.en: So it's, but the people that have gone through that process seem to have taken it on themselves and kind of own the word.
sentences.zh: 所以，但那些经历过这个过程的人似乎已经接受了它，并开始认同这个词。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So they're, they're owning it, they're doing it, but it's actually original.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在接纳它，正在使用它，但它实际上最初是……

sentences.en: Virginia was a, a derogatory term, right?
sentences.zh: 维吉尼亚，这是一个贬义词，对吧？

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Perhaps we need to think about rebranding.
sentences.zh: 也许我们需要考虑重塑品牌。

sentences.en: Um, but I guess whatever it is for now, it's just important that we talk about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我想无论它现在是什么，重要的是我们要谈论它。

sentences.en: And, you know, for me, who's, um, a qualified clinical psychologist to have never heard of this term, um, it was, you know, I'm, I'm, I wasn't excited to learn new terms and new
sentences.zh: 而且，对于我这个合格的临床心理学家来说，从未听说过这个词，嗯，你知道，我并不是不乐于学习新术语和新

sentences.en: things, but it feels like something I should have known about.
sentences.zh: 事物，但这感觉像是我应该知道的事情。

sentences.en: See, I don't think you should have done.
sentences.zh: 你看，我不认为你应该知道。

sentences.en: And I think that's the beauty of it in that this is the, this is the problem with hidden populations in that nobody should know, nobody would know that this exists within normal
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是它的美妙之处，因为这就是隐藏群体的问题所在，没有人应该知道，也没有人会知道在正常的

sentences.en: kind of consensus and normal kind of conversations in the same way that all those years ago, nobody knew that domestic violence was a thing.
sentences.zh: 共识和正常的对话中存在这种情况，就像多年前没有人知道家庭暴力是一回事一样。

sentences.en: Nobody knew that sexual violence was a thing or one of a violence was the thing.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道性暴力是一回事，或者某种暴力是一回事。

sentences.en: And it's the same rhetoric and going, it's not a, you know, it's not a hindrance on, on
sentences.zh: 这和那种论调一样，你知道，这并不是任何专业人士的障碍，

sentences.en: any professional to not know what it is when, for example, this is the first time the academic sphere can actually point themselves to an academic piece to say this exists.
sentences.zh: 不知道它是什么，因为例如，这是学术界第一次能够真正指出一篇学术文章来说明它的存在。

sentences.en: So I would never say that a professional should have known it.
sentences.zh: 所以我绝不会说专业人士应该知道它。

sentences.en: If anything, what it does is it adds to the professional repertoire of any professional working in, in the field to go, Oh, hang on a minute.
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，它所做的是增加了任何在这一领域工作的专业人士的专业储备，让他们意识到：哦，等一下。

sentences.en: Are we missing something out?
sentences.zh: 我们是不是漏掉了什么？

sentences.en: And that's the conversation, which I'm sure you're interested in.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们感兴趣的对话。

sentences.en: Um, so yeah, no, you know, no, no worries about not knowing it, but the beauty of being a professional is that once you do know it, you're like, Oh, I love that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，没关系，你知道，不用担心不知道它，但作为专业人士的美妙之处在于，一旦你知道了，你就会觉得：哦，我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I know it.
sentences.zh: 我知道了。

sentences.en: So thank you for introducing that to my, uh, my consciousness, but also it will be something
sentences.zh: 所以感谢你把它引入我的意识中，而且这也会成为我

sentences.en: that I honestly, sincerely will take with me to think about with, with clients, regardless of their faith, um, or current faith.
sentences.zh: 真诚地带入思考，并在与客户交流时考虑的事情，无论他们的信仰如何，或者当前的信仰如何。

sentences.en: Um, I guess having read your research, everybody should very interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想读了你的研究后，每个人都会觉得非常有趣。

sentences.en: Um, it was really, for me, it's so important to think about family systems, um, but also family backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对我来说，思考家庭系统以及家庭背景非常重要。

sentences.en: So, um, you know, you, you said that actually people who cast themselves in apostates and took part in your research, um, had experienced violence, um, from family members because
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你知道，你说过实际上那些把自己归为叛教者并参与你研究的人，确实经历过暴力，来自家庭成员的暴力，因为

sentences.en: of that.
sentences.zh: 这个原因。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, it's the same issues that you have where interfilm, intrafamilial kind of family violence is that kind of area where, you know, these, these, um, these victims
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这和你所面临的问题一样，家庭内部暴力就是这样一个领域，你知道，这些受害者

sentences.en: are being, as the kind of terms go, they're being assaulted, they're being seriously assaulted and they're being psychologically abused.
sentences.zh: 正如术语所说，他们正在受到攻击，受到严重的攻击，并且受到心理虐待。

sentences.en: You know, the difference between the assault and the serious assault is the difference between
sentences.zh: 你知道，攻击和严重攻击之间的区别在于

sentences.en: pushed and shoved to being threatened to be killed or be threatened to be harmed with, you know, like a knife or a gun or something, say it more serious than that.
sentences.zh: 推搡与被威胁杀害或被威胁用刀、枪或其他东西伤害之间的区别，所以比那更严重。

sentences.en: And psychological abuse contains the plethora of things like coercive control, stress, depression,
sentences.zh: 心理虐待包含了一系列事情，如强制控制、压力、抑郁、

sentences.en: isolation, you know, um, neglect, um, you know, all of those kind of, uh, terms as well, which
sentences.zh: 孤立、你知道，忽视，嗯，你知道，所有这些术语，我们

sentences.en: we, we see within the kind of clinical framework when we work, you know, I've got experience working
sentences.zh: 在临床框架内工作时都会看到，你知道，我有与经历过家庭暴力的人一起工作的经验，

sentences.en: with people that have been through domestic violence and it's very similar, um, kind of notions of the things that they've gone through.
sentences.zh: 他们所经历的事情与此非常相似。

sentences.en: Um, so yeah, it's, it's bringing on a seriousness in the fact that leaving a religious faith or
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，是的，这带来了一种严肃性，即离开宗教信仰或

sentences.en: making that decision that this perspective might not be for you has consequences that are very extreme.
sentences.zh: 做出这种观点可能不适合你的决定，会产生非常极端的后果。

sentences.en: And we need to be very aware of actually within certain frameworks, how is this working when they're going to the GP, when they go, you know, when families are going to the GP with
sentences.zh: 我们需要非常清楚，实际上在某些框架内，当他们去看全科医生（GP）时，当他们去，你知道，当家庭带着孩子去看全科医生时，

sentences.en: a child, when they're going to hospital, when they're seeing a nurse and they're seeing a midwife
sentences.zh: 当他们去医院，当他们看护士和助产士时，

sentences.en: in all these kinds of different areas or when they're going to school, you know, we only
sentences.zh: 在所有这些不同的领域，或者当他们去学校时，你知道，我们只需要

sentences.en: have to look at the kind of, um, we only have to look at the cases, the case studies of things
sentences.zh: 看看那些案例研究，比如维多利亚·克林比（Victoria Climbie）、

sentences.en: like Victoria Climbier, um, Baby P, Daniel Pelker in Coventry, you know, um, Sabji and Sujit Atwal,
sentences.zh: “婴儿P”（Baby P）、考文垂的丹尼尔·佩尔克（Daniel Pelker），你知道，萨布吉和苏吉特·阿特瓦尔（Sabji and Sujit Atwal），

sentences.en: you know, or Shafir Ahmed and look at the honor-based violence within that, all the different
sentences.zh: 你知道，或者沙菲尔·艾哈迈德（Shafir Ahmed），看看其中的荣誉犯罪，所有不同的

sentences.en: cultural and traditional issues and go, people in positions of power struggle to question that.
sentences.zh: 文化和传统问题，就会发现，处于权力地位的人很难质疑这一点。

sentences.en: Why did they struggle with that?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们很难质疑这一点？

sentences.en: And actually what's related to that?
sentences.zh: 实际上这与什么有关？

sentences.en: We've only just got to the point now where we were able to, where we've got systems in place for professionals to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们现在才刚刚达到能够建立系统让专业人士做到这一点的地步。

sentences.en: And now I'm basically saying, hi, you, you need to add another one into that, into that remit.
sentences.zh: 而现在我基本上是在说，嗨，你需要把这一个也加到那个职责范围内。

sentences.en: And here's something for, sadly for professionals, here's another, here's another
sentences.zh: 对于专业人士来说，很遗憾，这是另一个角度，我们需要意识到这一点，

sentences.en: angle that we need to be, we need to be aware of because another thing for us to think about on our training, but really important to think about.
sentences.zh: 因为这是我们在培训中需要考虑的另一件事，但确实非常重要。

sentences.en: Because you could, you could imagine them going to the GP with their, with their parent or with their carer and having gone through all of this
sentences.zh: 因为你可以想象他们带着父母或照顾者去看全科医生，经历了所有这些

sentences.en: stuff and not being able to voice it.
